what_it_does: Running large language models on devices requires storing weights (the model's learned parameters) in a compact format. Microscaling (MX) is a new number format that compresses floating-point values in groups, similar to how JPEG compresses images. This paper proposes a revised MX format with a new strategy called 'group direction' that makes compression work better with less information loss. To go with it, the authors designed specialized hardware (an accelerator) that understands and computes with this revised format efficiently. The hardware and software are co-optimized—designed together rather than separately—to run low-bit LLM inference faster.
